subject: literature
passage: Funmi had watched her mother sell fabric at the market in Lagos for years, but today the stall was hers for one hour. When a woman stopped to touch a roll of blue cloth, Funmi's voice came out as a whisper. She cleared her throat and tried again, louder this time, naming a price just as her mother would have. The woman nodded and counted out the money. Funmi folded the cloth with steady hands, grinning.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Funmi realizes that she would rather work somewhere other than the market.
choices.B: Funmi's mother nervously watches her daughter speak with a customer.
choices.C: Funmi overcomes her nervousness and makes a sale on her own.
choices.D: Funmi lowers the price of the cloth so that the woman will buy it.

explanation.why: At first Funmi's voice "came out as a whisper," showing she is nervous. She then speaks louder, names a price, makes the sale, and folds the cloth "with steady hands, grinning." The text as a whole shows her moving from nervousness to success on her own.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Funmi ends the text grinning; nothing suggests she wants to work elsewhere.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text never says the mother is present or nervous; the stall is Funmi's for the hour.
explanation.C: Correct. This covers the whole text: her nervous whisper at the start and her confident sale at the end.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Funmi names a price "just as her mother would have"; she does not lower it.
